steps.speaker: Black Screen
steps.content: █/█, 7:00 P.M., some venue in Eastside

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: You came.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: And Miss Matilda is here too. It's been days; the heroes of the West District look as dazzling as ever.
You see a familiar face the moment you enter the venue.
The man is neatly dressed and full of vitality today, a world away from how he looked a week ago.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You clean up nice.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: Well, it's a formal occasion after all. I thought I should dress up a bit.
Just then, a middle-aged man enters the venue. When Frank sees the man, he smiles and excuses himself.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: Sorry, I've got some business to attend to. Excuse me.
Frank walks up to the man in long strides and whispers in his ear. As he does so, you notice them looking your way a few times, both wearing a self-pleased expression.
After their brief exchange, the middle-aged man walks over to the front row.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Do you know that man?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Reagan, the current Deputy Speaker, valued by the Speaker for his fund-raising ability.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Heh, looks like they've decided to drop the act.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Well, they have achieved their goal.
More people flood into the venue. You notice a man giving a nod of acknowledgment to Matilda.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Who is that?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Kadis Cavendish, my distant cousin, currently Ms. Bernadette's right-hand man.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Some cousin. Didn't even come over and say hi...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, is he the representative of the Cavendish family at this hearing?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Yes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Ms. Bernadette is not coming?
As more and more people flood into the venue, some murmurs reach your ears.

steps.speaker: Noise
steps.content: Hey, did you see that? Bernadette is a no-show. Is she admitting defeat to the Speaker?

steps.speaker: Noise
steps.content: What else could it be? Obviously, they're making that poor girl a scapegoat.

steps.speaker: Noise
steps.content: That's a shame. Looks like the old man's re-election is a done deal. I was hoping she would be elected and reshuffle the City Council.

steps.speaker: Noise
steps.content: Look on the bright side. At least this way, the Cavendish family is bound to take a hit. If Councilor Bernadette wants to save her own skin, she'll have to do more than let a girl take the blame.

steps.speaker: Noise
steps.content: You're right. Gotta make her cough up what she's swallowed over the past two years.

steps.speaker: Noise
steps.content: Heh, it's only been a few years since the Abel incident, and Bernadette still has her sights on the Speaker's position... I don't think the Cavendish family will be able to come back from this ever again.
Gradually, you notice, all eyes in the room are being trained on Matilda.
Feigned sympathy, ill-concealed hatred, and more often than not, pure schadenfreude... Some of them even begin to look at Matilda as if evaluating a commodity.
You have no doubt that the former Executive Committee adjutant sitting next to you can also sense those unpleasant stares.
You place your hand on Matilda's shoulder.
The girl turns to you, and the smile she gives you is pure and genuine.
You realize that she's been ready all along.

As an elderly judge walks up to take his place behind the podium, the gazes on Matilda are slowly drawn away. A silence quickly falls over the venue, punctuated only by the clicking of camera flashes and the occasional cough.

You learned about the identity of the judge beforehand from the intelligence department. He is the Speaker's elder brother, who was swiftly promoted to his current position after his predecessor died in an "accident."

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Heh, in the end, neither the Speaker nor Ms. Bernadette showed up. But it seems that the Speaker's side is well-prepared.
The judge cuts short your mockery of him. He clears his throat and turns on the microphone.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Ahem, the purpose of this hearing is to clarify the events that have occurred in the West District over the past year and discuss the City Council's future plans and actions regarding the region.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Given that the Executive Committee has failed to achieve the expected goals in its reconstruction work in the West District, it is necessary and obligatory for all government agencies in Eastside to reflect on the overall policy concerning the West District.
The judge's eyes sweep around the venue, and only after confirming that the attention of all the attendees is on him, does he continue:

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: I declare, the hearing has now begun.
The judge has hardly put down the microphone when a young politician at the front stands up to speak.
The show begins.

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: Greetings, Judge. I'm Mensa, an official of the city's Treasury Department.

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: As we all know, the Treasury Department has been under tremendous pressure over the past year to support the City Council's series of measures in the West District.

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: Normally, I'd cite data and reports, but I've decided to forego that step, since this hearing is about problem-solving.

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: On behalf of my colleagues and the four million taxpayers in Eastside, I would like to ask the City Council the following questions:
The young councilor looks around the room and continues:

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: First question: The City Council claims that the Executive Committee was established to replace the ineffective Public Security Bureau. Specifically, it was established following the Keylan Square incident to bring the West District, commonly known as Syndicate, back on track.

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: But... In just one short year, billions have gone into the restoration of order in the West District, without anything to show for it. If anything, the entire region seems to have grown more chaotic.

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: May I ask what explanation the City Council, the most vigorous facilitator of the establishment of the Executive Committee, would give to the people of DisCity?
This standard line of questioning directed at the Speaker-led City Council, assertive and forceful, can certainly "represent" the voice of the majority of people who care about the future of DisCity.
However, you know that it's just a carefully orchestrated show.
Sure enough, the spokesman for the Speaker, Reagan, makes no move at all. The city official sitting next to him adjusts his glasses and stands up.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: First of all, I would like to make one thing clear to you. The West District is a lawless zone that has long been controlled by illegal violent groups.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: This has always been how the City Council characterizes the West District. It was in the past, it is now, and it seems that it will be for a long time to come.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: The West District was in chaos before the City Council green-lighted the establishment of the Executive Committee. And the causes of the chaos were the incompetence of the local security precinct in the region and the ineffectiveness of the West District Order Management Regulations!

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: To deal with the criminals and rioters, we had to use unconventional means...

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: Sorry to interrupt.

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: Are you saying that the Executive Committee did nothing wrong, and that they should've stepped up their effort by bringing in more chariots and machine guns to... clean up the West District?
The young councilor frowns, seemingly reluctant to utter the words "clean up."

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: Your description of the Executive Committee's method is not accurate, but the basic idea is right.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: In the early stages of their execution of the plan, the Executive Committee achieved great results. They eradicated gangs and other illegal organizations, and successfully restored some order to the West District.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: And then serious dereliction of duty occurred within the Executive Committee.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: Some Executive Committee officials lapped up the rhetoric of the so-called "progressives" and attempted to obstruct law enforcement. They advocated establishing "channels of communication" and solving problems in a "peaceful manner" by working with a group of rioters, gangsters, and ruffians.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: That was undoubtedly a betrayal.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: It was these despicable traitors who jeopardized the interests of Eastside; they betrayed the Executive Committee's internal information to a West District organization called Rustfire, which eventually led to the failure of the Executive Committee's operations in the West District.
The remark causes uproar in the crowd.
Some of them may be hearing it for the first time, and their surprise is real, but the vast majority are just acting surprised.

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: Sir, that's a very serious allegation you just made there. Is it the official opinion of the City Council?

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: Yes, it is.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: What I just said is not unfounded, nor is it an attempt to shift the blame. It is what actually happened in the West District.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: As for the details... Miss Matilda Cavendish, you don't mind providing them for our benefit, right?
Once again, all eyes are on the girl next to you.
Aside from you, everyone in the room seems to bear Matilda ill will, if the looks they give her are anything to go by.
Before you can say anything, Matilda gives you a determined look.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: The prosecution... no, um... Witness Matilda Cavendish, please take the stand.
The sleepy judge on the platform mumbles incoherently. This old man would probably have fallen asleep, you think to yourself, if he hadn't been called upon to continue with his duties.
Matilda stands up and walks over to take the stand.

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: Miss Cavendish, please introduce yourself before testifying and swear that you will tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, and that everything you're going to say is free of any form of coercion.
The young official places emphasis on the word "Cavendish."
Your gaze involuntarily drifts toward the spokesman for the Cavendish family. He is quietly flipping through a file, seemingly unconcerned about Matilda.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I, Matilda Cavendish, hereby swear that everything I am going to say at this hearing is free from any form of coercion. It is factual information as I observed it while serving as an adjutant to a frontline Executive Officer of the Executive Committee.
Matilda speaks into the microphone, her voice calm and resolute.

steps.speaker: Young official
steps.content: Then, Miss Cavendish, please enlighten us about what exactly happened in the West District.
Matilda takes a deep breath. Then she speaks in a calm, even voice:

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The failure of the Executive Committee, from what I saw, had nothing to do with the so-called "internal dereliction of duty," as the city official makes it out to be. And it's utterly absurd to talk about "traitors."

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The failure of the West District Reconstruction Committee was inevitable. The only explanation is that its action plan was outdated and completely wrong!

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Chariots and machine guns did not deter the people of the West District; instead, they united them. Rustfire, the most prominent organization in the region, gained unprecedented influence because of this!
The crowd falls silent after Matilda's brief remarks for a moment and then erupts.

steps.speaker: Noise
steps.content: The Cavendish girl is losing it. Is she trying to take her family down with her?!

steps.speaker: Noise
steps.content: How I wish Bernadette was here. I'd die to see her face when she hears this.

steps.speaker: City Official
steps.content: Nonsense! The Executive Committee did eradicate a large number of violent organizations in the West District in the beginning. You cannot deny this!
Among the din of the crowd, the voice of the city official sounds particularly harsh.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: About the eradication of violent West District organizations... Don't you think the accounts of those who were there carry more weight than the readings of a couple of reports by someone in Eastside?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, under the FAC, was deeply involved in the events related to the violent organizations in the West District, and the Chief of the Bureau...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: ...is here with us.
For some reason, the crowd quiets down.
Matilda looks at you with a determined gaze.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: You're... the Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I have something to add regarding Miss Matilda's statement and the doubts I sense from the audience.
The crowd falls silent, their eyes on you.
The judge squints his eyes and, after a moment, gives you permission to speak with a wave of his hand.
You take the microphone, look around, and begin to speak:

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: First of all, I would like to clarify one thing to you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The Executive Committee had nothing to do with the eradication of violent organizations in the West District.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The West District was indeed a lawless zone, but only up until last August. And it's not the Executive Committee who put an end to the chaos, but an organization called the Legion.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: After the appearance of the Square Black Ring, almost all major gangs in the West District were wiped out. A new equilibrium was established, and the people of the West District—chief among them the Drifter Camp—were starting to rebuild their homes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: However, as someone who has always been on the front line, I can responsibly tell you that the arrival of the Executive Committee did help the establishment of this new order tremendously.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A period of turbulence and friction followed the establishment of the Executive Committee, but it didn't last. The people of the West District reached a consensus: rather than waiting for the Executive Committee to come rolling in, they decided to set aside their differences and joined hands to drive away their common enemy.
You look around the room again and appreciate the miscellaneous reactions registering on their faces.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Of course, the City Council can choose to up the stakes by pouring more money into the bottomless pit.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And we'll see how destructive the power of the eight million people of the West District can be when they are forced to unite for a common cause.
Your speech seems to have caused the temperature inside the legislative hall to suddenly drop a few degrees. You can't help but feel pleased by the faces frozen in varying degrees of surprise.
Matilda gives you a small nod, her way of saying thank you to you.
Before the city official can respond, the microphone is snatched from his hand by a grim-faced Reagan.

steps.speaker: Reagan
steps.content: What you just said is alarmist. The City Council has obtained detailed information about Rustfire and has hand-picked a new team of extraordinary talent to address the situation.

steps.speaker: Reagan
steps.content: Once we eliminate this leading violent organization in the next operation, the situation in the West District will be completely reversed! The City Council...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Sorry...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Are you actually considering an all-out war with the West District?

steps.speaker: Reagan
steps.content: The West District is part of DisCity. This is an indisputable fact!

steps.speaker: Reagan
steps.content: If conflict can't be avoided, then it should be resolved as quickly as possible by force. The City Council will not tolerate any form of separatism in DisCity...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Wasn't it the City Council that signed the West District Order Management Regulations and left the eight million people of the West District to fend for themselves?
Reagan is lost for words. He gives Matilda a hostile look.
Giving Reagan no more attention, she scans the room and continues with her speech:

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Please open your eyes and take a good look at the situation.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: While the City Council has been obsessed with factional struggles, the West District has undergone a complete transformation.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The revival of the West District's mining industry has won them some bargaining chips. Capitalists, progressives, and even the Outlands have smelled the business opportunity and come to the negotiating table, hoping to get a share of the huge profits on the horizon.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Even so, the City Council is still bent on suppressing the West District by force and taking the whole cake.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Let's set aside for a moment the fact that the City Council's actions in recent years have caused some executive departments, such as the FAC, to drift away...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I just want to ask this question: Is the City Council really the highest authority in DisCity?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Will Paradeisos sit by and let a war break out between Eastside and the West District?
Complete silence...
Almost everyone in the room is stunned into a stupor by Matilda's speech. It's so quiet that you can hear their heavy breathing.
They've shut down like computers—a thousand of them—when their processing power is not enough to handle the information they've received.
The sound of hands clapping...
Sporadic applause rises from the back rows, where the reporters are.
A reporter stands up and speaks in a loud voice:

steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: Miss Cavendish, what do you think is the best course of action given the current circumstances?
Matilda answers the reporter's question without so much as a pause:

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Cooperation.
Her voice is calm and even, but it carries an undeniable note of determination.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Stop hostility, show goodwill. It's as simple as that.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Once upon a time, in the darkest days, DisCity, hailed as the last hope for human civilization, was built with the West District as the starting point.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: This wouldn't have been possible without the contribution of the West District miners.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Yet for many years now, the West District has been cut off from the rest of DisCity because of the Mania problem. Is this fair?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Is it fair to label the people of the West District as a destabilizing factor? They are sons and daughters of DisCity, just like the rest of us.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: They have gone through the darkest, most bleak night. Now, they can see the light and have the chance to start anew... As compatriots from across the river, shouldn't we lend them a helping hand?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Eastside should make overtures as soon as possible and repair its relationship with the West District, even if it's just for the sake of its own interests.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Or we'll be forced to watch the Hypercube from the new mines flowing into the Outlands. How is that going to benefit Eastside in any way?
The progressives in the corner, who have been silent up to this point, seem to have found hope. They whisper to each other frequently, and when they look at Matilda, there is eagerness in their eyes.
The Speaker's faction, on the other hand, falls silent.
After a while, Deputy Speaker Reagan takes the microphone and says in a slow but tyrannical tone of voice:

steps.speaker: Reagan
steps.content: I see, so this is the Cavendish family's stand on the matter?
The discussion veers away from such lofty topics as "Eastside's destiny" and "Eastside's future."
Now it's once again a game of politics, pure and simple.
Just then, Kadis Cavendish, Matilda's distant cousin and the spokesman for the Cavendish family, speaks up in an even voice...

steps.speaker: Kadis
steps.content: Miss Matilda's statement fully represents the position of the Cavendish family...
Silence again...
Reagan's face is wearing a gloomy expression. Kadis continues:

steps.speaker: Kadis
steps.content: Two days ago, an aid convoy from the Cavendish family crossed the Rust, and began negotiations with the West District forces led by Rustfire...

steps.speaker: Kadis
steps.content: Earlier today, we reached a preliminary consensus and agreed to cooperate with each other...

steps.speaker: Kadis
steps.content: One area of cooperation concerns the reopening of the West District mines, which you are most concerned about. The Cavendish family has successfully invested in it, on the condition that we donate materials and heavy equipment needed for the mining process.

steps.speaker: Kadis
steps.content: Of course, although the Cavendish family calls for setting aside differences and establishing cooperation, the above actions were not taken in the name of the City Council and will not affect the City Council's future plans for the West District.

steps.speaker: Kadis
steps.content: So, this is the Cavendish family's position on the matter, and Ms. Bernadette's too.
Dahlia Guide
Then the reporters in the back join in. Very soon, almost everyone in the room, except for Reagan and his followers, is applauding.
At least a third of the attendees, you notice, are trying to contact their families or factions with their terminals, without taking too long a break from their applauding.
They understand that someone has taken the first bite of the cake meant to be shared.
Time waits for no one.

steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: Just now, the representative of the Cavendish family claimed that they have gone into partnership with the West District, and mentioned that they have reached a preliminary agreement on the extraction of resources from the West District mines.

steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: This could mean that the West District, which has been in chaos for many years, is finally starting to get back on track...
When you access a news streaming room on your terminal, you are overwhelmed by a barrage of comments that cover almost every inch of the screen.
Public opinion is in your favor. You turn off the terminal.

The dust has settled, and Reagan is nowhere to be found. Ironically, now that he is gone, some of the Speaker's followers are quick to play the "traitor"; they take out their terminals and get to work.
Without saying another word, Matilda steps down from the platform.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: No, we won.
Matilda gives a tired smile. The speech she just delivered must have taken a heavy toll on her, so much so that even this landslide victory can't lift her spirits.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Or should I say it's a victory worthy of your perfect aunt?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She really is... ahead of her time.
Before Matilda can say anything in response, a male voice pipes up from behind you.

steps.speaker: Kadis
steps.content: Miss Matilda, Councilor Bernadette missed today's hearing because she had an aid convoy to arrange.

steps.speaker: Kadis
steps.content: But she will come back to Eastside soon and is hoping to meet with you.

steps.speaker: Kadis
steps.content: Chief of the MBCC, Councilor Bernadette would like to invite you too; she wants to express her gratitude in person to you for taking care of Matilda.
Study of Cavendish Mansion's Guest Wing

steps.speaker: Kadis
steps.content: Please wait here for a moment. Councilor Bernadette will be with you shortly.
The man leaves. You and Matilda are alone in the study.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You see, I was right when I told you to have faith in your aunt.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She went to the West District. At least in this regard, your aunt is better than the vast majority of councilors and politicians in Eastside.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: True self isn't unchangeable, is it?
To your surprise, Matilda shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Ms. Bernadette's true self has never changed.
Under your surprised gaze, Matilda continues:

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: If my performance at today's hearing had not been to my aunt's satisfaction...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Kadis would probably have swooped in to save the day. He could've announced to everyone that the Cavendish family had obtained intelligence on the Rustfire leadership and had launched a precise and rapid strike...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: "The Cavendish family will not waver in its determination to protect the interests of the Eastsiders and to confront any violent group that dares to disrupt the rules of DisCity."

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Something along those lines...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But she's your aunt...
This girl, who comes from a political family, looks calm.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Why is that any surprise, Chief? Her last name is Cavendish.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: A long time ago, I had a conversation with Ms. Bernadette, right here in this study...

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Are you sure about your choice?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Yes, Aunt Bernadette.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I understand why you want to do this.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: But the Executive Committee is not a good choice.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I know...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: But... Aunt Bernadette, I want to go to the West District, no matter what, to see what it is really like. I...

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: What the West District is really like is not important, never has been.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Considering the benefits we're currently garnering from the West District, as well as the risks you may face there, I'd advise you not to go. You could surely find a more suitable position here in Eastside.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Anyway, since your mind is made up, I should stop trying to convince you to stay.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I hope you can find your value in the West District.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I see...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: That might've been the moment when my target diverged from that of Ms. Bernadette.
You're on the verge of asking a question when the crisp sound of footsteps from outside the door interrupts you.

An elegant blonde lady pushes open the door and enters the study. At long last, you see the youngest female councilor of the City Council, a role model for the women of Eastside, and the de facto leader of a well-established political family...
Bernadette Cavendish.
She shakes your hand. After a brief exchange of greetings, Bernadette takes a seat at her desk.
She has a measured, self-assured smile that also seems enigmatic.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Thank you for taking care of Matilda, especially at today's hearing.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I couldn't make it due to a matter that needed my attention. It's thanks to your support that we were able to achieve such a satisfactory result.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Oh, it's nothing. Councilor, you taking the first step toward cooperation with the West District... now, that's something truly commendable.
The councilor smiles. This exchange of pleasantries ends smoothly.
Bernadette turns to look at her niece.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I questioned your choice once. But it has surprised me how much you've grown.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Sorry, Aunt Bernadette, I should've visited you more often.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: No need for such formality between us.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: You've proven your worth to me and the family, Matilda.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: As things stand, the Cavendish family is now one step closer to returning to center stage. However, more challenges will also come our way.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: There are a lot of things that Kadis can't handle. I need a personal assistant to help deal with them.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I need you by my side, Matilda.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: In return, you'll get a seat on the council after next year's elections.
This is a golden ticket to the corridors of power. You examine Councilor Bernadette's beautiful face, which doesn't betray her true age or emotions. It is wearing a sincere smile now.
What awaits her, however, is a sincere apology.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I'm very sorry, Aunt Bernadette.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I don't think I'm mature enough. I'm afraid I can't come back to work for you.
As you stare at the councilor's face, your gaze happens to meet hers.
After a moment, in a measured voice the councilor says:

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I see...

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Are you sure about your choice?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Yes, Aunt Bernadette.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Hmm... the MBCC is a nice place, and its Chief is an excellent superior worth following.
You can't detect any negative emotions on the councilor's face. Her gaze remains gentle and composed.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Well, I won't get in your way.
The councilor stands up.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I'm sure you have a lot of things to deal with, Chief. I'm sorry for taking up so much of your time.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: I think it's time to say goodbye.
What a straightforward way to say goodbye. You and Matilda stand up as well.
As you and Matilda make to leave, the councilor suddenly remembers something and calls out Matilda's name.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Matilda...

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: So, have you found your true self?
Matilda gives a smile, her most joyful one of the day.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Yes, I have.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Really? That's great.

steps.speaker: Bernadette
steps.content: Well, I'm looking forward to the day when our paths cross again.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I feel the same way, Aunt Bernadette.
